mechanism_found: A duplicated IGZ record IS instantiated when (1) the copy occupies a slot the count-bounded head walk already visits (same-size replacement of an existing node; insertion shifts every later walker by one record), and (2) a constructed predecessor points at it (reflection rebases the link; it does not construct the pointee). Run m3-…-1789301273731: PlacementReference 0x123138 copied over its successor 0x1231A8 — six words changed — loads and plays with the copy constructed (class 0x8049C738) and post-load-processed like an original; two live instances coexist in the chain. Why every earlier attempt failed: the first subjects were the level-init SCRIPT (type-92 = compiled scripts, singletons), appended copies fall outside every walked span, in-span insertions are stomped by the enclosing table record`s blob walk (type-52 0x40 stride) or desynchronise the count-bounded head walk, and growing the header table shifts all objects.
